key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks mapped HDPE friction stir welding quality, identifying 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating as optimal within the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process selection for HDPE joints by predicting thermal and force responses and distinguishing defective from defect-free welding windows.
method: Developed a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, force, material flow and defect formation.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Evaluated rotational speed, welding speed and bottom preheating to generate process maps.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N and raised peak temperature from 70 °C to about 100 °C.
watch_item: Predictive reliability beyond the tested HDPE welding parameter space requires further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
